items.prompt: Read: 'The nocturnal owl sat silently on the branch all day, opening its eyes only after the last light faded from the sky.' (A) What does nocturnal mean? (B) Write the exact phrase from the sentence that helped you figure out the meaning.
items.answer: (A) Nocturnal means active at night. (B) The clue phrase is 'opening its eyes only after the last light faded from the sky,' which shows the owl becomes active when it is dark.

steps: Read the entire sentence and look for clues about when the owl is active.
The owl sat silently all day (inactive) and opened its eyes only after the last light faded (at night).
The phrase 'after the last light faded from the sky' signals nighttime activity.
Nocturnal = active at night, resting during the day.

items.prompt: The word unpredictable has the prefix un- and the root predict. (A) What does predict mean? (B) What does un- add to the meaning? (C) Write a complete sentence using unpredictable correctly.
items.answer: (A) Predict means to say what will happen before it occurs. (B) Un- means 'not,' so unpredictable means not able to be predicted. (C) Example: 'The weather in spring is unpredictable because it can change from sunny to snowy in one day.'

steps: Predict = say in advance what will happen.
un- = not.
unpredictable = not able to be predicted or guessed ahead of time.
A good example sentence shows a situation that is hard to predict.

items.prompt: Read: 'Many scientists were amazed that such a transparent material — you could see right through it — could also be strong enough to stop a bullet.' (A) What does transparent mean? (B) Identify the clue phrase in the sentence. (C) Explain in your own words why the clue helps.
items.answer: (A) Transparent means see-through. (B) The clue phrase is 'you could see right through it.' (C) The author defines the word right inside the sentence using a dash, which tells the reader exactly what transparent looks like.

steps: The sentence uses dashes to set apart an explanation: 'you could see right through it.'
That phrase defines transparent directly.
This is called an 'appositive' or 'inline definition' — a clue type where the author explains the word in the same sentence.

items.prompt: The word misinterpret has the prefix mis-. (A) What does interpret mean? (B) How does mis- change its meaning? (C) Give a real-life example of when someone might misinterpret something.
items.answer: (A) Interpret means to understand or explain the meaning of something. (B) Mis- means 'wrongly,' so misinterpret means to understand something incorrectly. (C) Example: You might misinterpret a text message and think your friend is angry, when she was just in a hurry.

steps: interpret = to figure out the meaning of something.
mis- = wrongly or incorrectly.
misinterpret = understand incorrectly.
A real-life example should show a misunderstanding caused by reading something the wrong way.

items.prompt: Read: 'The flexible rubber band stretched around the whole stack of papers without snapping.' (A) What does flexible mean? (B) What is the root word inside flexible? (C) How does knowing the root help you figure out the meaning?
items.answer: (A) Flexible means able to bend or stretch without breaking. (B) The root is 'flex,' which means to bend. (C) Knowing that flex means bend helps you understand that flexible means something is able to be bent, and the suffix -ible confirms it means 'able to.'

steps: Context clue: the rubber band 'stretched without snapping,' showing it can bend a lot.
Root: flex = to bend.
-ible = able to be.
flexible = able to be bent or stretched.

items.prompt: A glossary entry reads: 'migrate (verb) — to move from one region or habitat to another, especially as seasons change.' Read this sentence: 'Monarch butterflies migrate each year, traveling up to 3,000 miles from Canada to Mexico.' Using BOTH the glossary and the sentence, explain what migrate means in your own words and give one detail from the sentence that supports the definition.
items.answer: Migrate means to travel from one place to another, especially when the seasons change. A supporting detail is 'traveling up to 3,000 miles from Canada to Mexico,' which shows the butterflies moving a very long distance to a different region.

steps: Glossary: migrate = move from one region to another as seasons change.
Sentence detail: 'traveling up to 3,000 miles from Canada to Mexico' shows long-distance movement.
Both sources agree: migrate means a seasonal journey to a different place.

items.prompt: Read: 'The nutritious school lunch — packed with protein, vegetables, and whole grains — gave the students energy for the whole afternoon.' (A) What does nutritious mean? (B) Identify the two clue types used in this sentence (context clue and/or word part). (C) Write a sentence using nutritious about a food you enjoy.
items.answer: (A) Nutritious means healthy and good for the body, providing what the body needs to grow and have energy. (B) Context clue: 'packed with protein, vegetables, and whole grains' and 'gave the students energy' show that nutritious = healthful. Word part: the root 'nutri' relates to nourishment. (C) Example: 'Apples are nutritious because they have vitamins and fiber that keep your body healthy.'

steps: Context clues: the foods listed (protein, vegetables, whole grains) and the effect (energy for the afternoon) define nutritious.
Word root: nutri comes from Latin meaning nourish.
nutritious = providing nourishment, good for health.

items.prompt: The word reformation is built from re- (again) + form (to shape) + -ation (the act of). (A) What does reformation mean? (B) How does each part contribute to the full meaning? (C) Give an example of a reformation.
items.answer: (A) Reformation means the act of forming or shaping something again, often to improve it. (B) re- = again; form = to shape or organize; -ation = the act or process of. Together: the act of shaping again. (C) Example: A school reformation might change the rules and schedule to help students learn better.

steps: Break the word: re- + form + -ation.
re- = again; form = shape; -ation = the act of.
reformation = the act of shaping or organizing something again.
Examples usually involve improving a system or organization.

items.prompt: Read this multi-sentence passage: 'The ancient cave paintings were discovered deep inside a cliff. Scientists believe they were made more than 17,000 years ago by early humans who used natural pigments.' (A) What does ancient mean? (B) Write every phrase or word from the passage that helped you determine the meaning. (C) Could you use a glossary to check your answer? How?
items.answer: (A) Ancient means very old, from a long time ago in the past. (B) Clue phrases: 'more than 17,000 years ago' and 'early humans' both signal something from the very distant past. (C) Yes — you would look up 'ancient' in the glossary alphabetically under A, read the definition, and compare it to your context-clue guess.

steps: 'More than 17,000 years ago' is a direct time clue showing extreme age.
'Early humans' also signals a very distant past.
Ancient = very old, from the far past.
A glossary check: find the A section, locate 'ancient,' read the definition, confirm it matches.

items.prompt: Read: 'The miniature model of the city was so detailed that you could see tiny windows in each skyscraper, but the whole model fit on one table.' (A) What does miniature mean? (B) Explain two different clues in the sentence that support your answer. (C) Use miniature in a sentence about something you have seen or used.
items.answer: (A) Miniature means a very small version of something. (B) Clue 1: 'tiny windows in each skyscraper' shows the model has very small details. Clue 2: 'the whole model fit on one table' shows the entire city was made small enough to fit on a single table. (C) Example: 'At the museum I saw a miniature train set with tiny houses and trees that looked like a real town.'

steps: Clue 1: 'tiny windows' — details are very small.
Clue 2: 'fit on one table' — an entire city on one table must be very small.
miniature = a very small version of something larger.
A personal example sentence shows understanding of the word's meaning.

items.prompt: The word unhelpfulness is built from un- + help + -ful + -ness. Break down each part and explain what the whole word means. Then write a sentence using it.
items.answer: un- = not; help = to assist; -ful = full of or having the quality of; -ness = the state or condition of being. Together: unhelpfulness = the state or condition of not being helpful. Example: 'The store worker's unhelpfulness made it hard for the customer to find what she needed.'

steps: un- = not.
help = assist.
-ful = having the quality of.
-ness = the state of being.
unhelpfulness = the state of not being helpful.
A sentence should show a situation where someone or something failed to help.

items.prompt: Read: 'Because the material was transparent, scientists could observe the chemical reaction happening inside the container without opening it.' (A) What does observe mean in this sentence? (B) What context clues helped? (C) What does transparent contribute to the meaning of the whole sentence?
items.answer: (A) Observe means to watch or look at carefully. (B) Clue: 'could observe... without opening it' shows they watched from outside the container. (C) Transparent explains HOW they could observe — the container was see-through, so they did not need to open it to see inside.

steps: observe = watch carefully.
Clue for observe: 'without opening it' means they watched from the outside.
transparent = see-through, which made outside observation possible.
The two words work together: transparent enables observation.

items.prompt: A glossary entry says: 'dissolve — to cause a substance to become part of a liquid so that the two cannot be separated by sight.' Read: 'She stirred the powder into the juice until it dissolved completely.' (A) Using the glossary, explain in your own words what happened in the sentence. (B) What word in the sentence confirms the glossary definition?
items.answer: (A) The powder mixed into the juice until it could no longer be seen separately from the liquid. (B) The word 'completely' confirms that the powder fully became part of the liquid, matching the glossary's 'cannot be separated by sight.'

steps: Glossary: dissolve = become part of a liquid, no longer visible.
Sentence: the powder was stirred in 'until it dissolved completely.'
'Completely' matches 'cannot be separated by sight' — full disappearance into the liquid.

items.prompt: The word prepackaged has the prefix pre- (before) + packaged (put into a package). (A) What does prepackaged mean? (B) How is it different from just 'packaged'? (C) Give a real-life example of a prepackaged item.
items.answer: (A) Prepackaged means packaged before you buy or use it — already put in a container or wrapper ahead of time. (B) 'Packaged' just means put in a package; 'prepackaged' adds the idea that this was done in advance, before the customer arrives. (C) Example: A prepackaged sandwich at a convenience store was wrapped before you bought it.

steps: pre- = before; packaged = put in a package.
prepackaged = packaged before you need it.
The difference: packaged = the act; prepackaged = done in advance.
Real-life examples include snack bags, juice boxes, and ready-made meals.

items.prompt: Read this passage: 'The rare fern grows only in moist, shaded forests. Its fronds are delicate and fragile — a single strong wind can tear them.' (A) What does fragile mean? (B) Identify the clue type used (context clue, word part, or both). (C) Explain why the author used a dash before 'a single strong wind can tear them.'
items.answer: (A) Fragile means easily torn, broken, or damaged. (B) Context clue: 'a single strong wind can tear them' shows that very little force breaks the fronds. This is a context clue. (C) The author used the dash to add an explanation or example right after the word fragile, so the reader understands it immediately without needing a dictionary.

steps: Context clue: 'a single strong wind can tear them' — minimal force causes damage.
fragile = easily damaged or broken.
The dash signals that what follows explains or gives an example of fragile.
This is an author's technique: defining a hard word right in the text.
